html:
An Israeli company, founded in 1965 at Kibbutz Hatzerim in the Negev desert, that turned drip irrigation into a worldwide industry.

Drip irrigation feeds water a drop at a time straight to the roots of each plant through thin plastic tubes with small outlets. Far less is lost to evaporation and runoff than with flooding fields or sprinklers, and fertiliser can be added to the water. The engineer Simcha Blass had worked out a design for a reliable dripper. He sold the rights to the members of the kibbutz, a collective farm community of the kind that began with Degania.

Cheap plastics made the idea practical. Drip lines let Israel farm the desert and use treated waste water, and Netafim became the world leader in the field, selling in over a hundred countries. Drip irrigation spread in India, China, California and Africa, wherever water is short. Alongside the center pivot it is one of the main irrigation inventions of the 20th century. In 2017 a Mexican chemical group bought most of the company.
sum: An Israeli company, founded in 1965 at Kibbutz Hatzerim in the Negev desert, that turned drip irrigation into a worldwide industry.
